label: copy phase: re-input of d/n (from 4th output on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or <DEL>), only on fed-back tokens (in_first=0), and almost only from recall_idx>=3 (output steps 4 onward), mostly in long sequences (L=8-9 hold 85% of the mass). It is strongly token-selective on the fed-back input: d (13x lift, 46% of mass) and n (6.5x, 21%), then weaker k, a, o, w, 2, c, i; it is essentially silent on other tokens. Input d/n at recall_idx>=3 covers about 66% of activation mass, but only ~9% of those steps fire. The cause is not found: adding the token being output (c/a/n/y are enriched) or the previous input (h/r/2) raises precision only to ~14-17% and loses recall. The largest activations are on d/n in L=9 sequences at recall_idx 3-5 (t=12-13). Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.011).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=17: d, k, n, a; t=13: d, n, a, k; t=15: d, n, k, a) and the token being output (most: c, a, n, y, 2, j; least: h, e, x, m); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, recall_idx=3, L=3.
